handbook.mirage_projector.section.compac: Use Compact for tiny local holograms and desk-sized displays where footprint matters more than efficiency at large sizes.
Nominal targets: 10×10 px, 32 px Lift, 4 px Float, 1 source. Power multiplier: ×1.00.

Compact can overdrive beyond 10×10 with a strong Core, but its cost rises quickly. A Netherite Core can therefore rival the effective PU budget of a Field with Glass while still being less efficient for massive geometry.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.displa: Use Display as the balanced general-purpose single-source projector when Compact is too small but a specialised chassis is unnecessary.
Nominal targets: 32×32 px, 48 px Lift, 12 px Float, 1 source. Power multiplier: ×1.50.
Display reaches readable medium-sized holograms efficiently and can still overdrive when extra PU is available.
Use Field for one massive continuous planar image or large wall-scale display. It is the high-efficiency chassis for very large 2D geometry.
Nominal targets: 128×128 px, 144 px Lift, 24 px Float, 1 continuous Plane source. Power multiplier: ×4.00.
Field always uses one continuous image plane; it does not split the projection into a 3×3 grid.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.genera: The main projector screen controls presentation. Source workspaces decide what is projected: Image, Item Snapshot, Entity / Humanoid or Banner.

Crying Obsidian is renewable after you obtain a real block: place a Lava source directly above Crying Obsidian and leave space below. It can nucleate a downward Small Bud, then grow through Medium, Large and Mature stages; the first nucleation is deliberately the slowest step.

Without Silk Touch, Small/Medium/Large/Mature crystals drop exactly 1/2/3/4 Crying Obsidian Shards and Fortune does not increase them. Silk Touch preserves the current crystal stage for decoration or relocation.

An active Beacon can energize Crying Obsidian crystals. Small/Medium/Large transmit about 75%/50%/25% of the visual beam and remain zero block-light; Mature transmits 0% and owns Mirage virtual world light. In open space its baseline decay is half vanilla (15,15 / 14,14 / ... / 1,1); solid walls cannot be crossed, and extra distance required to route around obstacles is penalized more strongly for natural gradual shadows. Energized crystals can release thin purple residual rays.

Obsidian Spikes are crafted from 3 Crying Obsidian Shards, 2 String and 1 Stick. Their nine sharp points slow living creatures like a berry bush and deal 2 damage points (1 heart) on each successful hurt event while the victim moves through them.

Projectors now form one crafting family: build the Compact Mirage Projector first, upgrade it to Mirage Display, then specialize that Display into Wide, Tall, Prism or Field. There is no direct Compact-to-specialist shortcut.

Breaking a projector normally in Survival packs its complete saved state into the dropped machine. Crafting upgrades carry that state forward, including the installed Core, imported images/GIFs, cards, snapshots and presentation settings.
Standard Core base output is Glass 32 PU, Quartz 48 PU, Amethyst 64 PU, Diamond 96 PU and Netherite 128 PU. A loaded Core Booster preserves that Base PU and adds ×1.50 amplification.

Effective capacity = Core base PU × chassis multiplier × Core amplification. Chassis multipliers are Compact ×1.00, Display ×1.50, Wide ×2.00, Tall ×2.00, Field ×4.00 and Prism ×2.00. Standard Cores use ×1.00; loaded Core Boosters use ×1.50.

Chassis geometry, Lift and Float numbers are nominal efficiency targets, not hard walls. Going past nominal is legal if enough PU exists, but that component receives a squared overdrive penalty so the correct larger chassis remains much more efficient.

PU load is explicit: a non-empty projection pays 2 PU base; geometry pays about 1 PU per 16×16 projected pixels; Lift pays 1 PU per 16px; Float pays 1 PU per 2px; source complexity and enabled effects add small fixed costs. Each component is then overdrive-adjusted when it exceeds its chassis nominal target.

Ghost gives only a tiny efficiency rebate: floor(non-base gross PU × Ghost% / 3000). Even at the 90% Ghost maximum this can never save more than 3% of the non-base load, so transparency cannot be abused as a power strategy.

Scale, Lift and Float sliders are generated dynamically from the current effective PU budget. Their endpoint is the highest currently valid value, so you should not need to drag through an orange invalid range and search backward pixel by pixel.

Image assets are synchronized by SHA-256 asset ID. Static PNG/JPEG/WebP/BMP imports normalize to PNG; GIF keeps animation. Mirage detects format from file bytes, so renamed GIFs still animate and unsupported animated WebP/APNG are rejected instead of flattened.

Plane Image modes are explicit: Front shows only Front; Back shows only Back; Mirrored reuses Front as a mirror; Readable reuses Front with corrected rear orientation; Independent uses separate Front and Back assets. Clearance must also pass before rendering.
Use Prism for a freestanding display readable from several directions instead of a single flat front/back plane.

Prism always keeps four cardinal lateral faces (North/East/South/West), one image or GIF per face and no stacking mode. Per-face nominal geometry adapts to content: horizontal 80×32, vertical 32×80, near-square 48×48. Lift nominal 96 px, Float 12 px, power multiplier ×2.00.
Image and Banner modes expose world-cardinal North, East, South and West faces. Prism has no top or bottom image face. Each populated face contributes geometry load.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.tall.1: Use Tall for vertical signage, portrait art, banner-like displays and stacked content where height matters more than width.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.tall.2: Nominal targets: 32×80 px, 96 px Lift, 16 px Float. Power multiplier: ×2.00. Image Mode toggles one continuous SINGLE source or four equivalent 1×4 cells; SINGLE preserves aspect ratio and vertical content is naturally most efficient.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.tall.3: Image Mode toggles between one continuous tall image and a 1×4 stack. MULTI uses the same square-cell rule as Wide; Scale 80 gives 20×80 overall, preventing the old Tall-vs-Wide magnification mismatch.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.wide.1: Use Wide for horizontal signs, panoramas and side-by-side content. It is tuned for landscape geometry.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.wide.2: Nominal targets: 80×32 px, 64 px Lift, 12 px Float. Power multiplier: ×2.00. Image Mode toggles one continuous SINGLE source or four equivalent 4×1 cells; SINGLE preserves aspect ratio and horizontal content is naturally most efficient.
handbook.mirage_projector.section.wide.3: Image Mode toggles between one continuous wide image and a 4×1 layout. MULTI uses four equal square cells; Scale 80 gives a complete 80×20 layout of four 20×20 cells, matching Tall cell sizing.
